declarations.description:
Base class every component extends.

Kept intentionally thin: universal resets/properties and the registration
contract only. Behavior that not every component needs (open/close, focus
delegation, form association, ...) belongs in a mixin from `src/mixins`.
Custom events are dispatched as typed `Event` subclasses from
`src/events`, not through a generic base-class `emit()` helper — see
`src/events/modal-close.ts` for the pattern.

Classes never register themselves (ADR 0001, D1): `defineComponents()`
registers a subclass per prefix (`u-button`, `acme-button`, ...) and
hands it the tag names of its registration through `tagNames`.
declarations.name: DSBaseElement

members.name: componentName
members.description:
Name of the component in the catalog, without any tag prefix: the
registered tag is `<prefix>-<componentName>`. Every concrete component
sets it; abstract bases (e.g. `ButtonBase`) don't.

members.name: dependencies
members.description:
Components this one renders (ADR 0001, D2): `defineComponents()`
registers them too, and `tagFor()` resolves their tag. Never hard-code
another component's tag in a template, nor create one with
`document.createElement` — a brand's override would be bypassed.

members.name: forDesignSystem
members.description:
The class a design system registers for this component, given its
settings: this class by default. A component that depends on a setting
returns a subclass that applies it, and leaves this class unchanged:
`Icon` returns a subclass with the design system's `icons` over its own.
`designSystem()` calls it once per class, after choosing the brand's
override, so the subclass extends the override.

declarations.description:
Shared base of `button` and `button-link`: size, variant, appearance,
disabled state, click handling and styles. Abstract: extend `Button` or
`ButtonLink`. Focus is delegated to the native control, so `focus()` and
`autofocus` work on the host, and a negative `tabindex` on the host takes
it out of the tab order.

The button is the building block of the other components: a composite
renders it for every control that looks like a button (`tagFor(Button)`),
so a brand's button changes them all (ADR 0031). They set its tokens to
fit it: an outer rule beats its `:host` tokens.

declarations.description:
Shared base of the groups of choices, `radio-group`: a label, an optional
hint, the choices (the children of the host) and the error message.
Abstract: extend `RadioGroup`, or write a group with `items` and
`groupRole`. The label, the hint, the error and the form behavior are
those of `FieldBase` (ADR 0017).

The group is the form control: it submits `value` under `name`, and its
choices have no form behavior of their own. A `required` group can't be
submitted while `value` is empty. Its message is the browser's, from a
hidden native radio: give `error-message` to write it in the page's
language.

The label is the accessible name of the element of the group's role, in
the same shadow root.

members.default: { set: (name: string, active: boolean) => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return; } if (active) { this.internals.states.add(name); } else { this.internals.states.delete(name); } }, has: (name: string): boolean => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return false; } return this.internals.states.has(name); }, }
members.description:
Wraps `internals.states` so components can toggle `:state(x)` selectors
(e.g. `:state(open)`) instead of reflecting extra boolean attributes.

`:state()` styling must stay an enhancement — reflect an attribute too
when the state is needed for the component to look right.

declarations.description:
Shared base of the comboboxes: a form field whose control opens a popup
below it, `autocomplete` for instance. Abstract: extend `Autocomplete`, or
write a combobox with `renderCombobox()` and `renderPopup()`. The label,
the hint, the error and the form behavior are those of `FieldBase`.

Its state is that of `comboboxReducer()` (`state/combobox.ts`, ADR 0010):
whether the popup is open, which of its items is active, whether it follows
what the user types. The base sends it the events of the control, and
shows the popup it describes.

The control keeps the focus while the popup is open, and names the
popup's content with `aria-controls`: both are in the same shadow root
(ADR 0009). The popup is a `popover="manual"` in the top layer, anchored
by an `AnchoredPopoverController`, with an animated entry and exit.

Keys of the control, popup closed: ArrowDown and ArrowUp open it and enter
it at its first or last item, Alt+ArrowDown opens it without entering.
Popup open: Escape and Alt+ArrowUp close it, Tab closes it and moves on;
the others, but Escape, go to `handlePopupKeydown()`. The popup also closes when the
focus leaves the field, when the field is disabled or read-only, and when
its form is reset. Escape closes only the popup, not a modal around the field.

A polite live region (`AnnounceController`) announces each new
`popupStatus`, the number of suggestions for instance: the popup's content
changes without the focus moving.

declarations.description:
Shared base of the editable comboboxes of the APG: a text input, and a
list below it of the options that match the text. Abstract: `autocomplete`
keeps the text as its value, `combobox` restricts its value to the options
(ADR 0025). The label, the hint, the error and the form behavior are those
of `FieldBase`; the popup and its state are those of `ComboboxBase`; the
list is that of a `ListboxController`.

The options are `options`, or else the `<option>` children of the field.
The list shows `maxOptions` of them at most, 100 by default, and says how
many it doesn't show: the user types more to narrow it (ADR 0026).

The options can come from a server: `loadOptions` receives the text, 300
milliseconds after the user's last change, and resolves with the
options, shown as they come. A newer text aborts the request. While the
text is empty, or until the first answer, the list shows `options`. With
`filter="none"`, the application filters `options` itself instead: it
listens to `input`, reads `inputValue`, and sets `options`. Either way,
new options open the list while the user types.

Keys, list open: ArrowDown and ArrowUp move to the next and previous
option, looping at the ends; Enter picks the active one; Escape closes
the list and keeps the text; Home, End and the other keys edit the text.

While the user types, a live region announces the number of options that
match: `resultsMessage` writes it. A request that lasts more than half a
second shows and announces `loadingLabel`.

The browser's own suggestions (`autocomplete`) are off by default: they
would cover the list. Give `autocomplete` to have both.

declarations.name: fieldIds
declarations.description:
The `id` of the elements `FieldBase` renders in its shadow root, for what
refers to them: a list named by the label, a popup anchored to the control.

Shared base of the form fields, `text-field` and `textarea`: a label, an
optional hint, a native control and its error message. Abstract: extend
`TextField` or `Textarea`, or write a field with `renderControl()`. The
label stays in the shadow root of its control: an `id` doesn't cross a
shadow root (ADR 0007).

A field takes part in its form like a native control (`withFormControl`):
it submits `value` under `name`, blocks the submission while invalid,
follows the form's reset and a `<fieldset disabled>`. A `readonly` field
keeps its value and isn't validated.

Validation is the browser's, on the native control, plus
`setCustomValidity()`. The error shows once the user has changed the value
and left the field, or once validation has run (a submission attempt,
`checkValidity()`, `reportValidity()`), then follows each keystroke. The
message is the browser's, in the browser's language: give `error-message`
to write it in the page's language. A message set with
`setCustomValidity()` comes first.

Its `input` and `change` events are those of a native control, on the
host: frameworks bind `value` as they would on an `<input>` (`v-model` in
Vue).

In a single-line field, Enter submits the form, as in a native `<input>`:
the inner control has no form of its own, so the field does it
(`submitOnEnter()`).

A required field shows `requiredIndicator` after its label, and the
control is announced as required. Where every field of a form is
required, set `required-indicator=""` and say it once above the form.

Once the error shows, the host matches `:state(user-invalid)`, as a
native control matches `:user-invalid`: style the layout around the field
with it. An enhancement: browsers without `:state()` (Chrome before 125,
Firefox before 126, Safari before 17.4) don't match it, and the field
shows its error without it.

members.name: renderControl
members.description:
Renders the native control, between the hint and the error message. It
has `id="control"` (the label's `for`), `class="control"` (the styles)
and its own part. It binds `.value=${live(this.value)}`, `required`,
`readonly` (`readOnly`), `disabled` (`isDisabled`), `autocomplete`, its constraints,
`controlInvalid`, `controlDescribedBy`, `handleInput` and
`handleChange`. A single-line control also binds
`@keydown=${this.submitOnEnter}`.

members.name: submitOnEnter
members.description:
For the `keydown` listener of a single-line control: Enter submits the
form, as HTML's implicit submission does for a native `<input>`. With a
submit button in the form, the first one is clicked, unless it is
disabled: a component submit button submits on `click()`. Without any, it is submitted when this field is its only
single-line one. Does nothing for a key another listener has handled,
nor while an input method composes the text.

declarations.description:
Shared base of the modal dialogs, `modal` and `drawer`. Built on the
native `<dialog>`: the browser provides the backdrop, makes the rest of
the page inert, closes it on Escape and gives the focus back to the
element that had it. Abstract: extend `Modal` or `Drawer`, with their
sheets (ADR 0008, ADR 0022).

Open it from a button, without script: `<u-button commandfor="id"
command="--show-modal">`, or a native `<button>` with the same attributes.
The commands are `--show-modal`, `--close` and `--request-close`; the last
two take the button's `value` as `returnValue`. From script, call
`showModal()`, `close()` or `requestClose()`, or set `open`.

declarations.description:
Shared base of the pickers, `select` and `date-picker`: a form field whose
control shows the picked value, and opens a popup to pick another one.
Abstract: extend `Select` or `DatePicker`, or write a picker with
`displayText`, `openPicker()` and `renderPopup()`. The popup and its state
are those of `ComboboxBase` (ADR 0018, ADR 0023).

The control is a `role="combobox"` element, not a text input: the user
picks, and doesn't type. It shows `displayText`, or `placeholder`. Its
label isn't a `<label for>`, which names only a native control: the
control has `aria-labelledby`, and a click on the label focuses it.

Keys of the control, popup closed: ArrowDown, Enter and Space open it on
the picked value; ArrowUp and Home on the first item, End on the last. A
click opens and closes it. A `required` picker can't be submitted while
its value is missing; its message is the browser's, from a hidden native
control (`renderValidityProxy()`).

declarations.description:
Shared base of the popups anchored to a trigger: `menu`. Its popup is a
`popover="manual"` of its shadow root, in the top layer, placed by an
`AnchoredPopoverController` below its anchor, with an animated entry and
exit. Abstract: extend `Menu`, or write a popup with `popup` and `anchor`
(ADR 0021).

`open` opens and closes it, as do `show()`, `hide()` and `toggle()`, and
the commands of the same name from an invoker button: `--show`, `--hide`
and `--toggle`. Escape, a press outside the component and the focus
leaving it close it (`DismissController`). Each change fires `u-toggle`,
with its `reason`, but on the first render.

The trigger is a `button` (ADR 0031): declare `Button` in the subclass's
`dependencies`. The sheet of the base styles its `class="chevron"` and the
popup's transitions (`class="popup"`).

declarations.description:
Shared base of the controls with their label after them, `checkbox` and
`switch`: a native `<input type="checkbox">`, the control the base draws,
then the label, the hint and the error message. Abstract: extend
`Checkbox` or `Switch`, or draw another control with `renderIndicator()`.
The label, the hint, the error and the validation are those of
`FieldBase` (ADR 0017).

As a native checkbox, it submits `value` under `name` while checked, and
nothing otherwise. The `checked` attribute is the default state: the
form's reset restores it. A `required` control can't be submitted
unchecked.

A `readonly` control keeps its state: a click doesn't change it, and
assistive technologies announce it as read-only. A native checkbox has no
`readonly`: the base prevents the click.

Its `input` and `change` events are those of a native checkbox, on the
host.

declarations.description:
An alert component that displays a message to the user.

The icon of its variant comes first: the icon of the same name, from the
`icon` component of its registration. It's decorative: the variant is in
the role and the colors, and the message says it.

Its container is a live region (`role="status"` or `"alert"`, from
`variant`). Screen readers announce what is added to a live region, not what
it already held when it appeared, so the message is revealed 100 ms after
the alert is first rendered: an alert inserted with its message is
announced too. Until then the message is laid out (nothing moves) but
invisible. An alert a server rendered shows its message at once.

declarations.description:
A text field with suggestions: the list below the input shows the
suggestions that match the text, and the user picks one or keeps typing.
The value is the text, free: a suggestion only fills it, as `<input list>`
does. For a value restricted to the suggestions, use `combobox`. The
input, the list, its filter and its keys are those of
`EditableComboboxBase` (ADR 0025).

Enter without an active suggestion closes the list: the text is the
value, and the form may submit.

members.description:

when the application filters them itself.

members.description:
The largest number of options the list shows, the first ones that

members.name: loadOptions
members.description:
Loads the options for the text the user typed, from a server for
instance: they replace `options`, as they are, without `filter`. Called
300 milliseconds after the user's last change of the text, unless it
is empty. Abort the work when `signal` aborts: a newer text replaces it.
A rejection shows `options` again, and reaches the page's error
handlers: catch it to show an error to the user. Property only.

announces it while the user types, and the status line shows it when
the list shows only `shown` of them. Give it in the page's language.
Property only.

`FieldBase.renderControl()` (`id="control"`, `class="control"`). It binds
`aria-expanded=${this.comboboxExpanded}`,
`aria-controls=${this.comboboxControls}` and
`@keydown=${this.handleComboboxKeydown}`.

members.name: renderPopup
members.description: Renders the content of the popup, a list of options for instance.

members.name: #syncLoad
members.description:
A new text: the user's loads its options, after the delay. An empty
text, or one the application gave, shows `options` again.

members.name: optionText
members.description: The text the input shows once the user picks `option`: its value by default.

members.name: renderOption
members.description: Renders the content of an option: its label, or its value. Override it for a richer content.

members.name: handleInput
members.description: The text changed: `FieldBase` takes it as the value, then the popup follows it.

members.name: handleTextChange
members.description:
For `renderCombobox()`: the `change` listener of the input, when the
user leaves it after changing the text. `handleChange()` by default.

members.name: handlePopupKeydown
members.description:
Handles a key of the control while the popup is open, other than
Alt+ArrowUp and Tab. Escape reaches it, then closes the popup. Returns whether it handled it: the base
then prevents its default. Handles none by default.

members.name: selectOption
members.description:
Called when the user picks an enabled option, by a click or Enter.
Fires `u-select`, then, unless canceled, gives the field the option's
value, as a user's change: `input`, then `change`. The list closes; the
focus stays in the input.

members.name: open
members.description:
Whether the popup is open. Reflected. Follows the real state: it turns
`false` when the user closes the popup. Set to `true`, it opens only
with some content to show.

members.name: renderControl
members.description:
Renders the control, from `renderCombobox()`, then the popup with the
content of `renderPopup()`, then the live region of `popupStatus`.

members.name: comboboxExpanded
members.description: For `renderCombobox()`: the `aria-expanded` of the control.

members.name: controlText
members.description: The text of the control, that the popup follows: `value` by default.

members.name: comboboxState
members.description: The state of the combobox: `open`, `activeIndex`, `typed`. Change it with `dispatch()`.

members.name: dispatch
members.description: Sends an event to `comboboxReducer()`, and renders again when the state changes.

members.name: showPopup
members.description: Opens the popup, if it has content. The keyboard enters it at `entry`.

members.name: popupShown
members.description: Called once the popup shows, placed: a popup that takes the focus gives it here.

members.name: hidePopup
members.description: Closes the popup, after its exit transition.

members.name: handleComboboxKeydown
members.description:
For `renderCombobox()`: the `keydown` listener of the control. A key
neither the popup nor the base handles is the field's: Enter submits the
form (`submitOnEnter()`).

members.name: popup
members.description: The popup, once rendered.

members.name: #control
members.description: The native control, once rendered.

members.name: formAssociated
members.description: Takes part in its form: value, validity, reset, `<fieldset disabled>`.

members.name: name
members.description: Name of the value in the form's data. Reflected: the form reads the attribute.

members.name: value
members.description:
The value, submitted with the form. The `value` attribute is the
default value: the form's reset restores it.

members.name: required
members.description: The form can't be submitted while the control is empty.

members.name: readOnly
members.description:
The user can't change the value; the form still submits it. Barred
from validation, as a native control: `required` doesn't apply.
Reflected to `readonly`: the browser reads the attribute.

members.name: form
members.description: The form of the control, or `null`.

members.name: validity
members.description: The validity of the value, as on a native control.

members.name: validationMessage
members.description: The message of the first constraint the value fails, `""` when valid.

members.name: willValidate
members.description: Whether the control is validated with its form: `false` while disabled or read-only.

members.name: checkValidity
members.description: Whether the value is valid. If not, fires `invalid`.

members.name: reportValidity
members.description: As `checkValidity()`, and the browser reports the error, focusing the control.

members.name: setCustomValidity
members.description:
Makes the value invalid with this message, as on a native control: a
check of the application, such as a username already taken. `""` makes
the value valid again.

members.name: updateValidity
members.description: Gives the host its validity, with `syncValidity()`, then shows its error.

members.name: customStates
members.default: { set: (name: string, active: boolean) => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return; } if (active) { this.internals.states.add(name); } else { this.internals.states.delete(name); } }, has: (name: string): boolean => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return false; } return this.internals.states.has(name); }, }
members.description:
Wraps `internals.states` so components can toggle `:state(x)` selectors
(e.g. `:state(open)`) instead of reflecting extra boolean attributes.
A no-op where `:state()` is unsupported (see `supportsCustomStates`), so
`:state()` styling must stay an enhancement — reflect an attribute too
when the state is needed for the component to look right.

control. For a control whose purpose the layout shows, the checkbox of
a table row for instance. The hint and the error still show. Reflected.

members.name: hint
members.description: A help text between the label and the control, read with the control.

members.description:
Shown after the label of a required field, and hidden from assistive

members.description: The `autocomplete` of the control: what the browser can fill in (`email`, `name`…).

members.description: The error message, in place of the browser's. Say how to fix the error.

members.description:
Read by assistive technologies before the error message, which a

members.description: Whether the user has changed the value, or validation has run, since the last reset.

members.name: error
members.description: The error message shown, `""` while none.

members.name: controlDescribedBy
members.description: For `renderControl()`: the `aria-describedby` of the control, the hint and the error shown.

members.name: controlInvalid
members.description: For `renderControl()`: the `aria-invalid` of the control, `"true"` while an error shows.

members.name: markInteracted
members.description: The user has changed the value: the error shows from now on, as after `change`.

members.name: submitOnEnter
members.description:
For the `keydown` listener of a single-line control: Enter submits the
form, as HTML's implicit submission does for a native `<input>`. With a
submit button in the form, the first one is clicked, unless it is
disabled: a component submit button submits on `click()`. Without any, it is submitted when this field is its only
single-line one. Does nothing for a key another listener has handled,
nor while an input method composes the text.

members.name: #messageOf
members.description: The message of the control's error, `""` while valid or read-only.

members.name: syncValidity
members.description:
Gives the host the validity of its value: by default, that of the native
control, the browser's constraints and ours. A field without a native
control overrides it (`ChoiceGroupBase`).

members.name: syncValueValidity
members.description:
For `syncValidity()` of a field without a native control: the value is
missing (`required` and empty), invalid with the message of
`setCustomValidity()`, or valid. A read-only field is valid. The message
of a missing value is `errorMessage`, or else that of the hidden native
control the field renders with `class="validity-proxy"` and `required`:
the browser's, in its language. `anchor` gets the focus on a failed
submission.

members.name: #showError
members.description: Shows the message of the host's validity, once the user has interacted.

members.name: hasError
members.description: Whether an error shows: for the layout of `render()`, and `aria-invalid`.

members.name: renderLabelContent
members.description: The label's text and the indicator of a required field.

members.description: The `<label>` of the control: `id="label"`, `for="control"`.

members.name: renderHint
members.description: The hint: `id="hint"`, hidden without `hint`.

members.name: renderError
members.description: The error message: `id="error"`, hidden while no error shows.

instance (ADR 0027). It is text, without a role nor any interaction: its

declarations.description:
A button that triggers an action, or submits or resets its form (`type`).
With `commandfor` and `command`, it controls another element without
script, like a native invoker button: it opens a `modal` with
`command="--show-modal"`.

A submit button sends its `name` and `value` with the form data, as a
native one does. The `submitter` of the `submit` event is a hidden native
`<button>` that carries them, removed once the event has run: a button of
a shadow root can't be the submitter of its host's form.

`click()` acts as a click on the inner button: it submits, resets or
sends the command. Implicit submission relies on it: Enter in a field
clicks the form's first submit button (`FieldBase.submitOnEnter()`).

With `loading`, a `spinner` covers the label and the button ignores
clicks, but keeps the focus: announce the end of the action in a live
region. With `popup`, it is the trigger of a menu or a dialog, and
`expanded` says whether that popup is open. With `expandable`, it shows
or hides a part of the page, and `expanded` says whether that part shows:
the application changes both on `click`. A button that stays pressed is
a `toggle-button`.
declarations.name: Button

cssParts.description: The `spinner` over the label, with `loading`.

declarations.description:
A calendar: the days of a month in a grid, to pick a date. It shows the
month of its `value`, or of today; the previous and next buttons, and the
keys, change the month. `date-picker` shows one in its popup (ADR 0023).

The grid follows the ARIA date picker: one Tab stop, on the focused day;
the arrows move by a day or a week, along the text direction; Home and
End to the start and end of the week; PageUp and PageDown by a month, by a
year with Shift. Enter, Space and a click pick the focused day: `value`
takes it, and the calendar fires `change`.

The names of the months and days, the full date of each day and the first
day of the week follow the language of the page (`lang`), through `Intl`.
A day outside `min` and `max` shows, but can't be picked.

declarations.description:
A group of checkboxes: the user checks any number of options among its
`checkbox` children. The group has the label, the hint and the error of
its options; the label, the hint, the error and the form behavior are
those of `ChoiceGroupBase` (ADR 0017).

The group submits the value of each checked checkbox under `name`, as a
`<select multiple>`: its checkboxes have no `name` of their own. `values`
holds them; `value`, the first one. The `checked` attribute of each
checkbox is its default state: the form's reset restores it.

A `required` group can't be submitted while no checkbox is checked. A
`disabled` or `readonly` group disables its checkboxes, or keeps their
state.

Its checkboxes fire their own `input` and `change` events: they reach the
group, and the page.

message. The user checks it to agree, or to pick an option among others
that don't exclude each other. For an option that applies at once, use

of `ToggleBase`.

selects all the others, while some of them are. The user's click clears

members.description:
Renders the native control, between the hint and the error message. It
has `id="control"` (the label's `for`), `class="control"` (the styles)
and its own part. It binds `.value=${live(this.value)}`, `required`,
`readonly` (`readOnly`), `disabled` (`isDisabled`), `autocomplete`, its constraints,
`controlInvalid`, `controlDescribedBy`, `handleInput` and
`handleChange`. A single-line control also binds
`@keydown=${this.submitOnEnter}`.

(e.g. `:state(open)`) instead of reflecting extra boolean attributes.

`:state()` styling must stay an enhancement — reflect an attribute too
when the state is needed for the component to look right.

members.description:

declarations.description:
A combobox: the user types to filter a list of options, and picks one.
The value is always one of the options, or `""`. The user types "par",
picks "Paris": the input shows its label, the form receives its value,
"75056". For a free text, use `autocomplete`; for a few options, without
typing, `select`. The input, the list, its filter and its keys are those
of `EditableComboboxBase` (ADR 0025).

Typing filters the options, and leaves `value` as it is. A pick sets it,
and fires `input`, then `change`. Emptying the input clears it at once,
with the `input` of the text; `change` follows when the user leaves the
field, as on a text input.

The user leaving the field ends the typing: the option whose label is the
text, if it is the only one, without case nor accents, is picked;
otherwise the input shows the label of `value` again. Escape, list closed,
shows it again too. Enter without an active option picks the option of
the text in the same way, and doesn't submit the form while the text
differs from the label of `value`.

`inputValue` holds the text, and `input` follows each change of it: with
`filter="none"`, the application reads it to fetch the options;
`loadOptions` fetches them for it. The options must hold that of `value`:
the input shows its label. Otherwise, the input shows the label of the
last option picked, or the value. With `loadOptions`, give the option of
the first value in `options`.

A `required` combobox can't be submitted while `value` is empty, whatever
the text. Its message is the browser's, from a hidden native `<select>`:
give `error-message` to write it in the page's language.
declarations.name: Combobox

members.description:

members.name: #picked
members.description: The last option picked: its label shows while the options no longer hold it.

members.name: optionText
members.description: The label of `option`.

members.name: syncValidity

members.name: renderCombobox
members.description:
Renders the control: `role="combobox"`, with the contract of
`FieldBase.renderControl()` (`id="control"`, `class="control"`). It binds
`aria-expanded=${this.comboboxExpanded}`,
`aria-controls=${this.comboboxControls}` and
`@keydown=${this.handleComboboxKeydown}`.

members.name: handleInput
members.description: The text changed: the popup follows it; an empty text clears the value.

members.description: For `renderControl()`: the `change` listener of the control.

members.name: handleComboboxKeydown
members.description: Enter and Escape end the typing; then the keys of `EditableComboboxBase`.

members.name: selectOption
members.description:
Called when the user picks an enabled option, by a click or Enter.
Fires `u-select`, then, unless canceled, gives the field the option's
value, as a user's change: `input`, then `change`. The list closes; the
focus stays in the input.

members.name: #commit
members.description: The user leaves the field: the option of the text, or the label of the value.

members.name: #optionOfText
members.description: The only enabled option whose label is the text, without case nor accents.

members.name: #textOf
members.description: The label of the option of `value`, of the last one picked, or the value.

members.name: dependencies
members.description: Renders the spinner of its status line with the `spinner` of its own registration.

members.name: options
members.description:
The options, as data: `{ value, label?, disabled? }`. Take precedence
over the `<option>` children. Property only.

members.name: filter
members.description:
Which options match the text, without case nor accents: those that
`contains` it, those that `starts-with` it, or all of them with `none`,
when the application filters them itself.

members.name: maxOptions
members.description:
The largest number of options the list shows, the first ones that
match: the user types more to reach the others. `Infinity` shows them
all.

members.name: loadOptions
members.description:
Loads the options for the text the user typed, from a server for
instance: they replace `options`, as they are, without `filter`. Called
300 milliseconds after the user's last change of the text, unless it
is empty. Abort the work when `signal` aborts: a newer text replaces it.
A rejection shows `options` again, and reaches the page's error
handlers: catch it to show an error to the user. Property only.

members.name: loadingLabel
members.description: What the status line shows and the live region announces while a request lasts.

members.name: resultsMessage
members.description:
Writes the number of options that match the text: the live region
announces it while the user types, and the status line shows it when
the list shows only `shown` of them. Give it in the page's language.
Property only.

members.name: handlePopupKeydown

then prevents its default. Handles none by default.

declarations.description:
A date picker: a form field whose control shows a date, and opens a
`calendar` below it to pick another one. The value is in the format of
HTML, `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `""`. To type a date, use `date-field`. The label,
the hint, the error and the form behavior are those of `FieldBase`; the
control is that of `PickerBase` (ADR 0023).

The control shows the date in the language of the page (`Intl`, `long`).
ArrowDown, Enter, Space and a click open the calendar, and give it the
focus, on the picked date or today. Its keys are those of the calendar.
A picked day closes it, fires `input` and `change`, and gives the focus
back to the control; so does Escape, without a change. Tab and a press
outside close it.

A disclosure: a summary the user presses to show or hide the content.
Built on the native `<details>` and `<summary>`: the browser gives the
button, its state, Enter and Space, and finds the hidden text with the
page's search (ADR 0020).

The details that share a `name` in the same document or shadow root form
an accordion: opening one closes the others, as native `<details name>`.
The component does it itself: `name` exists only from Chrome 120,
Firefox 130 and Safari 17.2, and doesn't cross the shadow roots.

It fires `toggle` when it opens or closes, as a native `<details>`: after
the change, without bubbling, whatever the cause.

The class a design system registers for this component, given its
settings: this class by default. A component that depends on a setting
returns a subclass that applies it, and leaves this class unchanged:
`Icon` returns a subclass with the design system's `icons` over its own.
`designSystem()` calls it once per class, after choosing the brand's
override, so the subclass extends the override.

members.name: language

declarations.description:
A file field: the user picks files, or drops them on its button, and the
form submits them (ADR 0028). Its control is a native
`<input type="file">`: its button opens the system's picker, and the
browser writes its text, in the browser's language.

Under it, a `tag-group` lists the files chosen, each with its name and
size (`fileMessage`), and a button that removes it: the user corrects a
choice of several files without picking them all again. A removal fires
`input`, then `change`.

The form receives each file under `name`. `required` needs a file.
`accept` filters the picker, as on a native input: the server checks the
files it receives. `value` is that of the native input, the name of the
first file after a fake path; `files` holds the files.

A read-only field shows its files, and changes nothing.

members.name: multiple
members.description: Whether the user can choose several files.

members.name: filesLabel

members.name: fileMessage
members.description:
Writes the text of a file in the list: its name and its size, in the
page's language, by default. The remove button's name holds it.
Property only.

members.name: chosen
members.description: The files chosen.

members.name: files
members.description: The files chosen, in order. Read-only: the user chooses them.

members.name: formValue
members.description: Each file under `name`, as a native file input submits them.

members.name: renderControl
members.description:
Renders the native control, between the hint and the error message. It
has `id="control"` (the label's `for`), `class="control"` (the styles)
and its own part. It binds `.value=${live(this.value)}`, `required`,
`readonly` (`readOnly`), `disabled` (`isDisabled`), `autocomplete`, its constraints,
`controlInvalid`, `controlDescribedBy`, `handleInput` and
`handleChange`. A single-line control also binds
`@keydown=${this.submitOnEnter}`.

members.name: handleInput
members.description: The user chose files: the field takes them.

members.name: #setFiles
members.description: Gives the native input `files`: the browser validates them, and the field shows them.

members.name: #remove
members.description:
The user removed `file`: as a new choice, `input` then `change`. The
list moves the focus to another file; after the last one, it goes to
the input.

members.name: #size
members.description: `size` bytes, in the unit that keeps it below 1000, in the page's language.

members.name: formAssociated
members.description: Takes part in its form: value, validity, reset, `<fieldset disabled>`.

members.name: name
members.description: Name of the value in the form's data. Reflected: the form reads the attribute.

members.name: value
members.description:
The value, submitted with the form. The `value` attribute is the
default value: the form's reset restores it.

members.name: required
members.description: The form can't be submitted while the control is empty.

members.name: readOnly
members.description:
The user can't change the value; the form still submits it. Barred
from validation, as a native control: `required` doesn't apply.
Reflected to `readonly`: the browser reads the attribute.

members.name: form
members.description: The form of the control, or `null`.

members.name: validity
members.description: The validity of the value, as on a native control.

members.name: validationMessage
members.description: The message of the first constraint the value fails, `""` when valid.

members.name: willValidate
members.description: Whether the control is validated with its form: `false` while disabled or read-only.

members.name: checkValidity
members.description: Whether the value is valid. If not, fires `invalid`.

members.name: reportValidity
members.description: As `checkValidity()`, and the browser reports the error, focusing the control.

members.name: setCustomValidity
members.description:
Makes the value invalid with this message, as on a native control: a
check of the application, such as a username already taken. `""` makes
the value valid again.

members.name: updateValidity
members.description: Gives the host its validity, with `syncValidity()`, then shows its error.

members.name: customStates
members.default: { set: (name: string, active: boolean) => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return; } if (active) { this.internals.states.add(name); } else { this.internals.states.delete(name); } }, has: (name: string): boolean => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return false; } return this.internals.states.has(name); }, }
members.description:
Wraps `internals.states` so components can toggle `:state(x)` selectors
(e.g. `:state(open)`) instead of reflecting extra boolean attributes.
A no-op where `:state()` is unsupported (see `supportsCustomStates`), so
`:state()` styling must stay an enhancement — reflect an attribute too
when the state is needed for the component to look right.

members.description: Disables interaction; also sets `aria-disabled="true"` on the host.

members.name: formDisabled
members.description: The browser's disabled state of a form-associated element.

members.name: styles
members.default: [(Base as unknown as typeof LitElement).styles ?? [], disabledStyles]

members.name: #formDisabledRender
members.description: The render of a disabled state the browser gave during an update.

members.name: getUpdateComplete
members.description: Also waits for the render of `formDisabledCallback()`.

members.description: The visible label, and the accessible name of the control. Required.

members.name: labelHidden
members.description:
Hides the label from the screen: it stays the accessible name of the
control. For a control whose purpose the layout shows, the checkbox of
a table row for instance. The hint and the error still show. Reflected.

members.name: hint
members.description: A help text between the label and the control, read with the control.

members.name: requiredIndicator
members.description:
Shown after the label of a required field, and hidden from assistive

members.name: autocomplete
members.description: The `autocomplete` of the control: what the browser can fill in (`email`, `name`…).

members.name: errorLabel
members.description:

members.description: Whether the user has changed the value, or validation has run, since the last reset.

members.name: error

members.description: For `renderControl()`: the `aria-describedby` of the control, the hint and the error shown.

members.name: controlInvalid
members.description: For `renderControl()`: the `aria-invalid` of the control, `"true"` while an error shows.

members.name: handleChange
members.description: For `renderControl()`: the `change` listener of the control.

members.name: markInteracted
members.description: The user has changed the value: the error shows from now on, as after `change`.

members.name: submitOnEnter
members.description:
For the `keydown` listener of a single-line control: Enter submits the
form, as HTML's implicit submission does for a native `<input>`. With a
submit button in the form, the first one is clicked, unless it is
disabled: a component submit button submits on `click()`. Without any, it is submitted when this field is its only
single-line one. Does nothing for a key another listener has handled,
nor while an input method composes the text.

members.name: #control
members.description: The native control, once rendered.

members.name: #messageOf
members.description: The message of the control's error, `""` while valid or read-only.

members.name: syncValidity
members.description:
Gives the host the validity of its value: by default, that of the native
control, the browser's constraints and ours. A field without a native
control overrides it (`ChoiceGroupBase`).

members.name: syncValueValidity
members.description:
For `syncValidity()` of a field without a native control: the value is
missing (`required` and empty), invalid with the message of
`setCustomValidity()`, or valid. A read-only field is valid. The message
of a missing value is `errorMessage`, or else that of the hidden native
control the field renders with `class="validity-proxy"` and `required`:
the browser's, in its language. `anchor` gets the focus on a failed
submission.

members.name: #showError
members.description: Shows the message of the host's validity, once the user has interacted.

members.description: Whether an error shows: for the layout of `render()`, and `aria-invalid`.

declarations.description:
An icon of the set of its registration, by name (ADR 0005).

The set of the base is `@unicorne/icons`: one module per icon, loaded the
first time an icon renders, so a page downloads only the icons it shows.
A component that draws an icon of the base in its own controls, a
chevron, bundles its markup with `Icon.bundle()`: the icon renders at
once, on a server too, and a page without that component downloads none.
The box keeps its size while the icon loads, and `updateComplete` resolves
once the icon is rendered. The icon takes the color of the text
(`currentColor`).

Without `label`, the icon is decorative: assistive technologies ignore it.
Give a `label` to an icon that carries meaning on its own.
declarations.name: Icon

members.name: icons
members.description:
The icon set: icon name → its SVG markup, or a loader of its module.
The default is the set of `@unicorne/icons`. A brand adds or replaces
icons by name in a subclass, registered with `overrides: { icon: … }`,
so every component of the registration renders them:
`static override icons = { ...Icon.icons, ...brandIcons }`.
Rendered as HTML: trusted markup only, such as the output of `unicorne-icons`.

members.name: bundle
members.description:
Gives the markup of icons of the base, by name, from the module of a
component that draws them: `Icon.bundle({ "chevron-down": chevronDown })`,
with `import chevronDown from "@unicorne/icons/chevron-down"`. While the
set holds the base's loader for that name, the icon renders this markup
at once, on a server too. A brand's icon of the same name still wins.

declarations.description:
An item of a `menu`: an action, or a choice (ADR 0021, ADR 0035). The
host has the role of its `type`; its content is its accessible name. Its
menu gives it the focus, and a click or Enter or Space on it fires its
`click`, then closes the menu.

`type="checkbox"` makes it a choice that toggles, `type="radio"` one
choice among the items of the same `name`: `menuitemcheckbox` or
`menuitemradio`, and `aria-checked`. A box shows the choice before the
label, as in a `select` with `multiple`. Space toggles it and keeps the
menu open; a click or Enter toggles it, then closes the menu. Each change
fires `change` from the item.

declarations.description:
A menu button: a button that opens a list of actions, its `menu-item`
children. The component renders its trigger, an `outlined` and `neutral`
`button` with `popup="menu"`: its control reports `aria-expanded` (ADR
0021, ADR 0031). `label` names the trigger and the menu. The popup and
its closing are those of `PopupBase`.

Keys of the trigger: Enter, Space and ArrowDown open the menu on its
first item, ArrowUp on its last. In the menu: the arrows move between the
enabled items, looping; Home and End reach the first and the last; typing
the start of a label moves to it; Enter and Space fire the item's `click`.
Escape and an item close the menu and give the focus back to the trigger;
Tab and a press outside close it.

members.description:
Asks to close the modal, like its close button and the `--request-close`

members.name: handleCommand
members.description:
Runs a command sent to the modal by an invoker button: `--show-modal`,
`--close` and `--request-close`. Override it to add commands, and call
`super.handleCommand(event)` for these.

members.name: focusInitial
members.description:
Gives the focus as the dialog's focusing steps would, across the slot:
to the content's `autofocus` element, or else to the close button.
Firefox and Safari only look for `autofocus` in the shadow root. Opened
on its first render, the modal has a close button without its native
`<button>` yet, and the dialog keeps the focus: focus again once the
element has rendered, unless the focus moved meanwhile.

members.name: requestCloseFor
members.description: Fires `u-cancel` for `reason`, then closes unless a listener canceled it.

members.name: handleDialogKeydown
members.description: Escape: the cause of the browser's `cancel`, which follows in the same task.

members.name: handleDialogCancel
members.description:
A close request of the system: Escape, or the back button or gesture
of Android.
Closes through `u-cancel` and the exit transition, not at once.

members.name: handleDialogClose
members.description:
Fires whenever the native <dialog> closes, regardless of cause — the
single place that keeps `open` truthful to the actual dialog state and
announces the closing.

members.name: isOutside
members.description: A click on the backdrop targets the dialog, outside its box.

members.name: handlePointerUp
members.description:
`closedby="any"`, in every browser: the dialog renders `closerequest`,
and the modal closes on a press outside itself, to give `u-cancel` its
reason. Safari has no `closedby`. Press and release outside: a text
selection that ends on the backdrop doesn't close it.

A banner of important information for the whole service, above its
header: an outage, a deadline (ADR 0034). In the `banner` slot of `page`.

It isn't a live region: present when the page loads, it reads as content,
before the header. The message says its nature, « Information : »,

message that appears after an action is an `alert` or a toast.

`u-close`. The application keeps the choice, and moves the focus to the
content: `page.focusContent()`.

declarations.description:
A number field: a label, an optional hint, a native `<input
type="number">` and its error message. The browser validates the number,
`min`, `max` and `step`, and its arrows and ArrowUp and ArrowDown step the
value. The value is the number as text, in the format of HTML (`3.5`), or
`""`. For a code made of digits (a postal code, a card number), use
`text-field` (ADR 0019).

With `formatOptions`, the field shows its number formatted in the
language of the page, `1 250,50 €`, while it doesn't have the focus
(ADR 0036). With the focus, the user edits the number alone, `1250,5`,
and writes it in the language of the page; a pasted `1 250,50 €` reads
too. The control is then a text input with `role="spinbutton"`:
ArrowUp and ArrowDown step the value, and a hidden native number input
gives the browser's validation of `min`, `max` and `step`. The value
stays in the format of HTML.

members.name: renderControl

The layout of a page: a notice, its header, its navigation beside its
content, and its footer (ADR 0034). One per page.

The content is the page's `main` landmark. A skip link comes first in the

narrower than `--u-page-navigation-inline-size` plus
`--u-page-content-min-inline-size`, the navigation goes above the
content: no media query.

A popover: a button that shows a panel of content below it, an
explanation, a few fields, a set of links. The panel is a non-modal
dialog: the page stays usable, and Tab goes from the button into the

the panel and gives the focus back to the trigger; a press outside and
the focus leaving the component close it too.

declarations.description:
A group of radios: the user picks one value among its `radio` children.
The group is the form control: it submits `value`, the `value` of the
checked radio, under `name`. The `value` attribute is the default value:
the form's reset restores it. The label, the hint, the error and the form
behavior are those of `ChoiceGroupBase` (ADR 0017).

Tab reaches the checked radio, or the first enabled one. The arrow keys
move to the next and previous enabled radios and check them, looping at
the ends, along the text direction; Space checks the focused radio. A
click checks a radio. A `readonly` group keeps its value: the arrow keys
move the focus only.

Its `input` and `change` events follow each change of `value` by the
user, on the group, as those of a native radio.

declarations.description:
A select: the user picks one value among its options, in a list below
the control. The value is always one of the options, or `""`: for a free
text, use `autocomplete`. The label, the hint, the error and the form
behavior are those of `FieldBase`; the control is that of `PickerBase`; the
popup and its state are those of `ComboboxBase`; the list is that of a
`ListboxController` (ADR 0018).

The options are `options`, or else the `<option>` children of the select.
The control shows the label of the selected option, or `placeholder`.

Keys, list closed: ArrowDown, Enter and Space open it on the selected
option; ArrowUp and Home open it on the first option, End on the last.
List open: the arrows, Home and End move the active option; Enter, Space,
Tab and Alt+ArrowUp pick it; Escape closes the list and keeps the value.
Typing the start of an option's label makes it active, and opens the
list.

A `required` select can't be submitted while `value` is empty. Its message
is the browser's, from a hidden native `<select>`: give `error-message` to
write it in the page's language.

Its `input` and `change` events follow each pick that changes `value`, as
those of a native `<select>`.

With `multiple`, the user chooses several options: Enter, Space and a
click choose an option or leave it out, and the list stays open. `values`
holds the chosen values, `value` the first one, and the form receives one
entry per value, as a `<select multiple>`. The `selected` of the
`<option>` children are the default choices.

Tab or Alt+ArrowUp. The list closes; the focus stays on the control. A

members.name: syncValidity

control, the browser's constraints and ours. A field without a native

members.name: renderValidityProxy

members.name: renderLabel

members.name: renderCombobox
members.description:
Renders the control: `role="combobox"`, with the contract of
`FieldBase.renderControl()` (`id="control"`, `class="control"`). It binds
`aria-expanded=${this.comboboxExpanded}`,
`aria-controls=${this.comboboxControls}` and
`@keydown=${this.handleComboboxKeydown}`.

members.name: open
members.description:
Whether the popup is open. Reflected. Follows the real state: it turns
`false` when the user closes the popup. Set to `true`, it opens only
with some content to show.

members.name: renderControl

Renders the control, from `renderCombobox()`, then the popup with the
content of `renderPopup()`, then the live region of `popupStatus`.

members.name: popupStatus
members.description:

the user can't see coming, the number of suggestions for instance.
Nothing by default.

The user can't change the value; the form still submits it. Barred

members.description: Whether the control is validated with its form: `false` while disabled or read-only.

members.name: checkValidity
members.description: Whether the value is valid. If not, fires `invalid`.

members.name: reportValidity
members.description: As `checkValidity()`, and the browser reports the error, focusing the control.

members.name: setCustomValidity
members.description:
Makes the value invalid with this message, as on a native control: a
check of the application, such as a username already taken. `""` makes
the value valid again.

members.name: updateValidity

members.name: customStates
members.default: { set: (name: string, active: boolean) => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return; } if (active) { this.internals.states.add(name); } else { this.internals.states.delete(name); } }, has: (name: string): boolean => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return false; } return this.internals.states.has(name); }, }
members.description:
Wraps `internals.states` so components can toggle `:state(x)` selectors
(e.g. `:state(open)`) instead of reflecting extra boolean attributes.
A no-op where `:state()` is unsupported (see `supportsCustomStates`), so
`:state()` styling must stay an enhancement — reflect an attribute too
when the state is needed for the component to look right.

members.description: For `renderControl()`: the `change` listener of the control.

members.description: The user has changed the value: the error shows from now on, as after `change`.

members.name: submitOnEnter
members.description:
For the `keydown` listener of a single-line control: Enter submits the
form, as HTML's implicit submission does for a native `<input>`. With a
submit button in the form, the first one is clicked, unless it is
disabled: a component submit button submits on `click()`. Without any, it is submitted when this field is its only
single-line one. Does nothing for a key another listener has handled,
nor while an input method composes the text.

members.name: #messageOf
members.description: The message of the control's error, `""` while valid or read-only.

members.name: syncValueValidity
members.description:
For `syncValidity()` of a field without a native control: the value is
missing (`required` and empty), invalid with the message of
`setCustomValidity()`, or valid. A read-only field is valid. The message
of a missing value is `errorMessage`, or else that of the hidden native
control the field renders with `class="validity-proxy"` and `required`:
the browser's, in its language. `anchor` gets the focus on a failed
submission.

members.name: renderControl
members.description:
Renders the native control, between the hint and the error message. It
has `id="control"` (the label's `for`), `class="control"` (the styles)
and its own part. It binds `.value=${live(this.value)}`, `required`,
`readonly` (`readOnly`), `disabled` (`isDisabled`), `autocomplete`, its constraints,
`controlInvalid`, `controlDescribedBy`, `handleInput` and
`handleChange`. A single-line control also binds
`@keydown=${this.submitOnEnter}`.

members.default: { set: (name: string, active: boolean) => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return; } if (active) { this.internals.states.add(name); } else { this.internals.states.delete(name); } }, has: (name: string): boolean => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return false; } return this.internals.states.has(name); }, }
members.description:
Wraps `internals.states` so components can toggle `:state(x)` selectors
(e.g. `:state(open)`) instead of reflecting extra boolean attributes.
A no-op where `:state()` is unsupported (see `supportsCustomStates`), so
`:state()` styling must stay an enhancement — reflect an attribute too
when the state is needed for the component to look right.

members.name: submitOnEnter
members.description:

form, as HTML's implicit submission does for a native `<input>`. With a

disabled: a component submit button submits on `click()`. Without any, it is submitted when this field is its only

members.description:
Wraps `internals.states` so components can toggle `:state(x)` selectors
(e.g. `:state(open)`) instead of reflecting extra boolean attributes.

`:state()` styling must stay an enhancement — reflect an attribute too
when the state is needed for the component to look right.

members.name: submitOnEnter
members.description:
For the `keydown` listener of a single-line control: Enter submits the
form, as HTML's implicit submission does for a native `<input>`. With a

disabled: a component submit button submits on `click()`. Without any, it is submitted when this field is its only

nor while an input method composes the text.

children, whose cells are `table-cell` and `table-header-cell` (ADR 0030).
Any row fits: a row of details across the columns (`colspan`), a group
heading, a cell holding links, buttons or a `badge`.

The rows with `slot="head"` form its header, which stays in view while
the other rows scroll under it. `label` is its caption and its name.

A header cell with `sort-key` sorts the rows: a press fires `u-sort`, then
the table shows the new sort, `aria-sort` and an arrow. The table keeps
the order of its rows: the application sorts them, with `sortRows()` or
on its server, and renders them again.

With `selectable`, each row gets a `checkbox` before its cells, named by
`selectMessage` and its row header; the head gets one for every row.
`values` holds the `value` of the rows selected; each choice of the user
fires `change`. A row without `value`, a row of details for instance, has
an empty cell there. The selection outlives the rows that go: a row of
another page, or one a filter hides, stays selected, and shows selected
again when it comes back. The head's box chooses the rows shown. The
application takes a deleted row out of `values`.

The table scrolls past the width of the page, and past
`--u-table-max-block-size`. While it scrolls, it takes the focus, for the
keyboard, as a region named by its caption.

declarations.description:
Tabs: a list of `tab` and their `tab-panel`, one panel shown at a time.
`value` is the `value` of the selected tab, and of the panel it shows
(ADR 0020).

Tab reaches the selected tab, then its panel. The arrow keys of the
orientation move to the next and previous enabled tabs and select them,
looping, along the text direction; Home and End select the first and last
tabs. A click selects a tab. Each selection by the user fires `change`.

A list wider than its tabs scrolls. Buttons at its edges scroll it, for
the pointer: they stay out of the Tab order and of the accessibility tree,
the arrow keys bring each tab into view (`OverflowController`).

The tabs and the panels are children of the host: the tabs go in the
`tab` slot by themselves. The component links each tab and its panel with
`aria-controls` and `aria-labelledby`, and gives them an `id` if they have
none.

members.name: renderControl
members.description:
Renders the native control, between the hint and the error message. It
has `id="control"` (the label's `for`), `class="control"` (the styles)
and its own part. It binds `.value=${live(this.value)}`, `required`,
`readonly` (`readOnly`), `disabled` (`isDisabled`), `autocomplete`, its constraints,
`controlInvalid`, `controlDescribedBy`, `handleInput` and
`handleChange`. A single-line control also binds
`@keydown=${this.submitOnEnter}`.

members.name: formAssociated
members.description: Takes part in its form: value, validity, reset, `<fieldset disabled>`.

members.name: name
members.description: Name of the value in the form's data. Reflected: the form reads the attribute.

members.name: value
members.description:
The value, submitted with the form. The `value` attribute is the
default value: the form's reset restores it.

members.name: required
members.description: The form can't be submitted while the control is empty.

members.name: readOnly
members.description:
The user can't change the value; the form still submits it. Barred
from validation, as a native control: `required` doesn't apply.
Reflected to `readonly`: the browser reads the attribute.

members.name: form
members.description: The form of the control, or `null`.

members.name: validity
members.description: The validity of the value, as on a native control.

members.name: validationMessage
members.description: The message of the first constraint the value fails, `""` when valid.

members.name: willValidate
members.description: Whether the control is validated with its form: `false` while disabled or read-only.

members.name: checkValidity
members.description: Whether the value is valid. If not, fires `invalid`.

members.name: reportValidity
members.description: As `checkValidity()`, and the browser reports the error, focusing the control.

members.name: setCustomValidity
members.description:
Makes the value invalid with this message, as on a native control: a
check of the application, such as a username already taken. `""` makes
the value valid again.

members.name: updateValidity
members.description: Gives the host its validity, with `syncValidity()`, then shows its error.

members.name: customStates
members.default: { set: (name: string, active: boolean) => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return; } if (active) { this.internals.states.add(name); } else { this.internals.states.delete(name); } }, has: (name: string): boolean => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return false; } return this.internals.states.has(name); }, }
members.description:
Wraps `internals.states` so components can toggle `:state(x)` selectors
(e.g. `:state(open)`) instead of reflecting extra boolean attributes.
A no-op where `:state()` is unsupported (see `supportsCustomStates`), so
`:state()` styling must stay an enhancement — reflect an attribute too
when the state is needed for the component to look right.

members.name: submitOnEnter
members.description:
For the `keydown` listener of a single-line control: Enter submits the
form, as HTML's implicit submission does for a native `<input>`. With a
submit button in the form, the first one is clicked, unless it is
disabled: a component submit button submits on `click()`. Without any, it is submitted when this field is its only
single-line one. Does nothing for a key another listener has handled,
nor while an input method composes the text.

control the field renders with `class="validity-proxy"` and `required`:
the browser's, in its language. `anchor` gets the focus on a failed
submission.

members.name: renderControl
members.description:
Renders the native control, between the hint and the error message. It
has `id="control"` (the label's `for`), `class="control"` (the styles)
and its own part. It binds `.value=${live(this.value)}`, `required`,
`readonly` (`readOnly`), `disabled` (`isDisabled`), `autocomplete`, its constraints,
`controlInvalid`, `controlDescribedBy`, `handleInput` and
`handleChange`. A single-line control also binds
`@keydown=${this.submitOnEnter}`.

members.name: checkValidity
members.description: Whether the value is valid. If not, fires `invalid`.

members.name: reportValidity
members.description: As `checkValidity()`, and the browser reports the error, focusing the control.

members.name: setCustomValidity
members.description:
Makes the value invalid with this message, as on a native control: a
check of the application, such as a username already taken. `""` makes
the value valid again.

members.description: Gives the host its validity, with `syncValidity()`, then shows its error.

members.name: customStates
members.default: { set: (name: string, active: boolean) => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return; } if (active) { this.internals.states.add(name); } else { this.internals.states.delete(name); } }, has: (name: string): boolean => { if (!supportsCustomStates || !this.internals?.states) { return false; } return this.internals.states.has(name); }, }
members.description:
Wraps `internals.states` so components can toggle `:state(x)` selectors
(e.g. `:state(open)`) instead of reflecting extra boolean attributes.
A no-op where `:state()` is unsupported (see `supportsCustomStates`), so
`:state()` styling must stay an enhancement — reflect an attribute too
when the state is needed for the component to look right.

members.name: submitOnEnter
members.description:
For the `keydown` listener of a single-line control: Enter submits the
form, as HTML's implicit submission does for a native `<input>`. With a
submit button in the form, the first one is clicked, unless it is
disabled: a component submit button submits on `click()`. Without any, it is submitted when this field is its only
single-line one. Does nothing for a key another listener has handled,
nor while an input method composes the text.

members.name: syncValidity
members.description:
Gives the host the validity of its value: by default, that of the native
control, the browser's constraints and ours. A field without a native
control overrides it (`ChoiceGroupBase`).

members.name: syncValueValidity
members.description:
For `syncValidity()` of a field without a native control: the value is
missing (`required` and empty), invalid with the message of
`setCustomValidity()`, or valid. A read-only field is valid. The message
of a missing value is `errorMessage`, or else that of the hidden native
control the field renders with `class="validity-proxy"` and `required`:
the browser's, in its language. `anchor` gets the focus on a failed
submission.

declarations.description:
A toaster: the short messages that follow an action, "Saved", in a corner
of the page, above everything else. One toaster per page; the application
calls `show()` (ADR 0022).

A message leaves after its `duration`, or when the user closes it. The
pointer resting on the messages, or the focus in them, holds them. Past
`max` messages, the oldest one leaves. Each closing fires `u-close`, with
the message's id and the `reason`.

A live region announces each message: politely, interrupting for a
`warning` or a `danger` one. The messages are in the top layer, a
`popover="manual"` shown while it has some.

declarations.description:
A button that stays pressed or released: the bold of a text editor, a
filter of a list (ADR 0032). `pressed` is its state, `aria-pressed` on
its native control. A click flips it, then fires `input` and `change`,
like a checkbox; setting `pressed` fires nothing.

Its label stays the same in both states: assistive technologies say the
state. A label that says the action instead ("Show the map", then "Hide
the map") belongs to a `button`.

Released, it is drawn like a `button`, `neutral` and `outlined` by
default. Pressed, the tokens of `toggle-button` paint it. In a `toolbar`,
the arrow keys move between its buttons.

declarations.description:
Reactive controller: shows a popover of the host's shadow root in the top
layer, below an element of the same shadow root, its anchor: the list of an
autocomplete, a menu, a tooltip (ADR 0009, D2).

Each `[popover]` of the shadow root is a `popover="manual"`: the component
decides when it closes (Escape, a click outside, a choice). The controller
sets `data-open` on it while it's open: the CSS writes its open state on
`[data-open]`, not on `:popover-open`, which the oldest browsers of the
matrix lack. With an exit transition, the open state is
`[data-open]:where(:not([data-closing]))`.

The popover sits below its anchor, aligned with its start edge, at least
as wide, and flips when it would overflow the viewport. Its block margin
is the space between them. Where CSS anchor positioning is missing, the
controller loads Floating UI and positions it from script: the popover also
shrinks to the space left, down to its `max-block-size`. Without the
Popover API, there is no top layer: the popover is fixed above the page
(`--u-z-index-overlay`), and an ancestor that clips its overflow clips it.

Out of the document, a popover leaves the top layer: the controller closes
those it opened when the host disconnects.
declarations.name: AnchoredPopoverController

members.name: #openings
members.description: The opening under way of each popover: a closing meanwhile cancels it.

members.name: #opened
members.description: The open popovers, and what stops the fallback's updates of each.

members.name: #offsets
members.description: The block margin of each popover: the fallback applies it as an offset.

members.name: isOpen
members.description: Whether `popover` is open: shown, or about to be once positioned.

members.name: open
members.description:
Shows `popover`, a `popover="manual"` of the shadow root, in the top
layer, anchored below `anchor`, an element of the same shadow root.
Resolves once it's shown and positioned. Already open, it only follows
the new anchor.

members.name: close
members.description: Hides `popover` at once: its exit transition, if any, runs before.

members.name: #follow
members.description:
Positions `popover` with Floating UI, then again on each scroll,
resize or move of the anchor, until it closes. Resolves once
positioned: before the next paint, so it never shows unpositioned.

Assistive technologies read what `announce()` gives it, without the focus
moving: the number of suggestions of a list, a page loaded, a message
saved. `ComboboxBase` creates one.

Render the region from the first render, with `render()`: a region added
with its text isn't announced. It stays empty until `announce()`.
declarations.name: AnnounceController

members.description: The text of the region.

members.name: announce
members.description:

last one is announced again. `""` empties the region, silently.

declarations.description:
Reactive controller: lets a component take commands from invoker buttons
(Invoker Commands, ADR 0008): a native `<button commandfor="id"
command="--name">`, or a component with `withInvoker` (`button`).

The browser runs a built-in command (`show-modal`) only on a native
`<dialog>` or popover, and never sends it to a custom element. A component
takes custom commands, prefixed with `--`.

`handle` runs a command sent to the component: `event.command` is its
name, `event.source` the button, retargeted to its host. Handle the
component's `--` commands and ignore the others: the polyfill also sends
built-in ones.

Where Invoker Commands are missing, the first connected component loads
invokers-polyfill: the page's native invoker buttons need it too.
declarations.name: CommandsController

declarations.description:
Reads the text direction of its host when it connects, and renders the
host again when it changed: a chevron that points back or forward follows
it. `:dir()` is missing before Chrome 120 and Firefox 126.

The first render, on a server too, is left to right: the direction is
known once the host is in the page.
declarations.name: DirectionController

a press outside the host and the focus leaving it each call `dismiss()`
with their `DismissReason`, while `active(reason)` is true. `ComboboxBase`
creates one, for Escape and the focus.

The component chooses the causes, and passes the reason on to its event.
A modal `<dialog>` doesn't need it: the browser dismisses it, and only the
dialog receives a press on its backdrop.
declarations.name: DismissController

or while the keyboard focus is in it. A short pass of the pointer shows
nothing; the pointer can move from the trigger to the popup, a
descendant of the host, without hiding it. `Tooltip` creates one.

The keyboard focus shows at once: `:focus-visible`, not a click. The

declarations.description:
Reactive controller: a list of options in the host's shadow root,
`role="listbox"`, whose active option follows the keyboard while the focus
stays on a control: the input of an autocomplete, the button of a select
(ADR 0009). The control takes `activeDescendant` as its
`aria-activedescendant`, and `id` as its `aria-controls`.

The controller connects a list to the DOM; it holds no state of its own.
The host owns the active index (`comboboxReducer()`, or
`moveIndex()` of `state/collection.ts`) and the options.

It also reads the `<option>` children of the host, as data, in
`childOptions`, and never changes them: a framework keeps rendering them.
Either way, the list renders its own copies, in the shadow root of the
control: `aria-activedescendant` only reaches an element of its own tree
(ADR 0007). `render()` also renders the hidden slot of these children.

On a server, the host has no children to read: a host rendered there
(ADR 0014) reads them after its first render, which then matches the
server's.
declarations.name: ListboxController

declarations.description:
Reactive controller: loads data for its host, from a server for instance,
one load at a time (ADR 0026). Each `load()` replaces the previous one:
it aborts its task, and drops its result. The host renders again at each
change of `pending`, `loading`, `slow` and `value`.

A task that rejects keeps `value` as it was cleared: `undefined`. The
error reaches the page's error handlers (`reportError()`), as an uncaught
one would. A task that handles its own errors resolves with what to show.

On a server, nothing loads: `load()` runs in the browser, after a user's
action.
declarations.name: LoadController

members.description: The delay before the task starts.

members.name: #slowTimer
members.description: The delay before `slow` turns `true`.

members.name: #abort

members.description: Whether a load waits for its delay, or runs.

members.description: Whether a task runs.

members.name: slow
members.description: Whether a task has run longer than `slowDelay`.

members.description: The result of the last task that resolved, `undefined` before it and after `clear()`.

members.name: load
members.description:
Starts `task` after the delay, unless another `load()` or `clear()`
comes first. Aborts the task that runs. `value` stays as it is until
the new task resolves.

members.name: clear
members.description: Aborts the load, and forgets `value`.

members.name: #cancel
members.description: Stops the delay and the task, without a render.

Reactive controller: tells whether the content of a scrolling container
goes past its start or its end, along the inline axis, and scrolls it.
`Tabs` creates one, to show its scroll buttons. It also tells whether the
container scrolls at all, along either axis: `Table` makes it focusable
then, for the keyboard.

It measures the container after each render of the host, when its size
changes (`ResizeObserver`) and when it scrolls, and renders the host
again when an edge changes. It works in either text direction.

Reactive controller: a roving tabindex over the items of a composite

focus to the next and previous enabled items, looping at the ends, along
the text direction. `RadioGroup` creates one.

The items are elements the user focuses: the hosts of `radio`, of their
own `role`. The controller sets their `tabindex` after each render of the
host: render the host again when the items change (`slotchange`).

before the table shows the new sort. The application sorts its rows, by
`key` and `direction`. Cancelable: `preventDefault()` keeps the sort
shown.
declarations.name: TableSortEvent

members.name: key

members.name: direction

declarations.description: Mixin: Adds disabled functionality

members.name: customValidity
members.description: The message of `setCustomValidity()`, `""` when none.

members.name: formValue
members.description: What the form submits under `name`: `value` by default.

members.name: updateValidity
members.description:
Gives the host its validity, after each render and after
`setCustomValidity()`. By default, only the message of
`setCustomValidity()` makes it invalid, unless it is read-only. A
component with a native control copies the control's validity instead
(`FieldBase`).

declarations.description:
Mixin: makes a component a form control, like a native `<input>`. It
submits `formValue` under `name`, takes part in the form's validation,
follows the form's reset and the browser's restoration of the page, and a
`<fieldset disabled>` (`withDisabled`).

Apply it over `withInternals` and `withDisabled`: it reads `this.internals`,
and a form control can be disabled.

A read-only control is barred from validation by the browser, as a native
one: `readonly` is reflected. The component renders its native control
`readonly` too, and changes nothing from the user's input.
declarations.name: withFormControl

members.name: formAssociated
members.description: Takes part in its form: value, validity, reset, `<fieldset disabled>`.

members.name: name
members.description: Name of the value in the form's data. Reflected: the form reads the attribute.

members.name: value
members.description:
The value, submitted with the form. The `value` attribute is the
default value: the form's reset restores it.

members.name: required
members.description: The form can't be submitted while the control is empty.

members.name: readOnly
members.description:
The user can't change the value; the form still submits it. Barred
from validation, as a native control: `required` doesn't apply.
Reflected to `readonly`: the browser reads the attribute.

members.name: form

members.name: validity
members.description: The validity of the value, as on a native control.

members.name: validationMessage
members.description: The message of the first constraint the value fails, `""` when valid.

members.name: willValidate
members.description: Whether the control is validated with its form: `false` while disabled or read-only.

members.name: checkValidity
members.description: Whether the value is valid. If not, fires `invalid`.

members.name: reportValidity
members.description: As `checkValidity()`, and the browser reports the error, focusing the control.

members.name: setCustomValidity
members.description:
Makes the value invalid with this message, as on a native control: a
check of the application, such as a username already taken. `""` makes
the value valid again.
